\item[] \textit{Note:} Log preferences, $\rho = 1$. The cost is that of equation \eqref{eq:esc:fGeneral}, $\ln f(\theta_t, \tau_t) = -\tau_t(1-\theta_t)\big[\lambda_1 M + \tfrac12\lambda_2\tilde V(1-\theta_t)\big]$, with $M = \sum_i\gamma_i|y_i-1|$ the amount the flat component carries and $\tilde V$ the dispersion of relative incomes; the linear cost sets $\lambda_2 = 0$ and the quadratic $\lambda_1 = 0$. The linear and the quadratic costs have one parameter each, calibrated so that the U.S.\ electorate re-elects its observed design $\theta^{\ast}$ with $(\beta, \omega)$ recalibrated at each trial value; the linear-quadratic cost has two, pinned jointly by the U.S.\ and the UK designs at $\kappa = \lambda_1/\lambda_2 = 0.129$, so that the UK\textquotesingle s own value is the U.S.\ one and France\textquotesingle s design is a prediction. $f(\theta^{\ast})$ and $f(0)$ are the shares of revenue that reach U.S.\ households at the observed design and at a flat benefit, at the 2020 tax rate. ``$\theta$ chosen'' is the design in 2020 on the economy\textquotesingle s own freely simulated path under the U.S.\ parameters; ``own value'' is the value of the parameter the specification calibrates ($\lambda_1$ under the linear cost, $\lambda_2$ under the others, at the U.S.\ $\kappa$ under the linear-quadratic) at which that path re-elects the observed design, with $\beta$ imposed from the U.S.\ and $\omega$ recalibrated at each trial value. France\textquotesingle s observed design is the corner $\theta = 1$, so its own value is the smallest at which its electorate chooses the corner, a bound ($\geq$); under the quadratic cost no finite value reaches it (--). The observed designs and 2020 tax rates are those of table \ref{table:US:Calib} and the dispersions of each economy are in table \ref{table:US_ESC:variantsCountry}; the UK is at its own income percentiles, and at the U.S.\ ones in the same table.
